articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.
These designations aim to disrupt financial networks supporting illicit drug trafficking and terrorist organizations globally.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, as well as the implications of these actions, are available on the OFAC website.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) reached a settlement agreement with Bank of America, N.A. on October 13, 2026, for apparent violations of numerous sanctions programs, including those related to Iran, Russia, narcotics, and global terrorism.
The settlement amount for these violations is $11,662,930.

Bank of America admitted to 475 apparent violations, which included channeling correspondent banking payments through blocked banks due to technical and human error, allowing designated individuals to make payments and withdraw funds due to poor sanctions alert calibration, failing to promptly update watchlists, and mishandling business accounts associated with blocked persons.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, ICC Designation, and Burma-related Removal
body: OFAC announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics on October 9, 2026, alongside a designation related to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and a removal from Burma-related sanctions.
The settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics addresses apparent violations of OFAC regulations.
Further details on the ICC designation and the specific Burma-related entity removed from the sanctions list are available in the official announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026.
This new general license provides specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under the Russia sanctions program.
The details of the authorized activities and any associated conditions are outlined in the official publication.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-related Designations, Issues New General Licenses for Iran and Amended Russia-related GL
body: OFAC announced new Iran-related designations on October 8, 2026, alongside the issuance of a new Iran-related General License and an amended Russia-related General License.
These actions reflect ongoing efforts to address Iran's destabilizing activities and to adjust existing sanctions programs.
The new Iran-related General License and the amended Russia-related General License provide specific guidance on permissible activities under the respective sanctions regimes.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designations Removals, Updates, and Publication of Iran-related Alert and FAQ
body: On October 5, 2026, OFAC announced several designations removals and updates, along with the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ).

The Iran-related Alert warns foreign financial institutions that they could be targeted at any time without advance notification if they continue to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions.
The amended Iran-related FAQ 156 clarifies how foreign financial institutions will be informed of potential sanctionable activity, removing previous language about advance contact.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new counter terrorism designations on October 2, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities identified as supporting international terrorist organizations.
The action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to disrupting the financial networks of terrorism worldwide.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-related Designations and Updates, Transnational Criminal Organizations Designation, and Publishes Determination and Amended FAQ
body: OFAC announced new Iran-related designations and designations updates on October 1, 2026, along with a designation targeting Transnational Criminal Organizations.
Additionally, OFAC published an Iran-related Determination and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question.
These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter Iran's illicit activities and disrupt criminal networks.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations Designations; Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: On September 30, 2026, OFAC announced new designations targeting Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations.
Concurrently, OFAC removed several designations related to Belarus, counter narcotics, and Libya.
These actions reflect a dynamic approach to sanctions, adding new targets while delisting others based on evolving circumstances.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: OFAC announced a series of new designations on September 29, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics, counter terrorism, Iran-related activities, and non-proliferation.
These comprehensive designations aim to disrupt various illicit networks posing threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests.
The actions underscore the U.S. government's broad strategy to combat a range of malign activities through financial sanctions.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined $11,662,930 by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a civil penalty of $11,662,930 against Bank of America, N.A. on October 13, 2026.
This penalty is part of a settlement agreement addressing apparent violations of various U.S. sanctions programs.
The violations included channeling correspondent banking payments through blocked banks and failing to properly screen for designated individuals and entities.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
